core_obligations: Identify the Cech groups (proof lines 1832-1845): using the companion lemma describing Cech cohomology by maps from representable objects, the author rewrites the Cech groups of the covering as groups of homomorphisms subject to compatibility conditions.

Kill the higher groups (proof lines 1845-1855): injectivity of I and the description of the relevant subsheaves allow the author to extend the compatible families, which shows that the higher Cech groups vanish.
Conclude (proof lines 1855-1859): the degree zero group is I(U) by the same description, so the Cech cohomology is concentrated in degree zero as asserted.
proof_roadmap: Rewrite the Cech groups through the description by maps from representable objects.
Use injectivity of the module to extend the compatible families, killing the higher groups.
Read off the degree zero group and conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the Cech cohomology of an injective module over a ringed site with respect to an arbitrary covering: it is I(U) in degree zero and vanishes in positive degrees (statement lines 1815-1830). The proof rewrites the Cech groups through the description by maps from representable objects (proof lines 1832-1845) and then uses the extension property of injective modules to kill the higher groups (proof lines 1845-1855), the degree zero case following from the same description (proof lines 1855-1859). The non-formal content is the use of injectivity in the form of extendability of compatible families. The claim is H2: one identification plus one extension argument.
